openings.claim: Challenge the hypothesis that magnetic attraction is necessary for retention. Magnetic success would establish an instance of M→B, not B→M; weaker spare attraction does not establish either implication universally.
openings.delta: Remove magnets as the retaining dependency. Bend and drill supplied strips into a locating pocket bolted through existing carriage slots, with side/face capture, stops contacting only unmarked regions, and a pivoting rear service gate. Cork pads take up play; positive boundaries carry stroke loads. Open the gate and withdraw using the broad face or unmarked rear edge.
openings.prediction: A geometrically feasible pocket could preserve ≤1 mm displacement for twenty strokes on the spare despite its 3 N magnetic release. The nearest rival, magnetic retention against cork without positive capture, instead depends on attraction/friction. Differing observations are displacement and release during identical spare-plate runs; no rival failure is assumed.
openings.probe: Compare two configurations: ordinary magnet/cork retention and the pocket with magnets absent. First verify exposed working edge, clearance, attached rails and undamaged plate/carriage. Use ruler/marker references, three twenty-stroke spare runs per configuration, checking displacement throughout; perform three timed removal/return checks per configuration wearing supplied thick gloves without touching the working edge. Log gate manipulation and seating failures within the twenty-minute observation allowance.
assumptions: Slot dimensions accept M4 fastening; strip width/thickness permits bending and adequate stiffness. These dimensions and stroke loads are unknown.
Available unmarked contact regions permit opposing stops and face capture entirely outside stroke clearance; pocket seating/play stays within 1 mm.
Supplied bolts/nuts suffice for mounting and a glove-operable gate; fabrication fits eighty minutes.

Defeat: no compliant pocket geometry, deformation or displacement above 1 mm, edge contact, or removal/return above sixty seconds. Insufficient comparison time leaves feasibility unestablished; a time cap alone is not an informative test.

assessment: One proposed counterexample probe removes magnetic dependence; it is not deployed or demonstrated. Unknown geometry and capacity prevent a preservation claim. Both configurations remain subject to every hard constraint.
